source: NCERT Class XI, An Introduction to Indian Art (Part 1), Ch. 5 (Later Mural Traditions).

sections.heading: 1. Mural Painting — Meaning
points: **Murals** = paintings made on **walls/ceilings** of caves and temples (as opposed to miniatures on paper).
Indian mural tradition spans roughly the **2nd century BCE to the 8th–10th centuries CE** and beyond.
Chief sites: **Ajanta, Ellora, Bagh, Sittanavasal, Badami, Armamalai, Lepakshi**.

sections.heading: 2. Ajanta — The Masterpiece
points: **Ajanta caves (Maharashtra)** — Buddhist rock-cut caves (chaityas and viharas); a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
The murals depict the **life of the Buddha and the Jataka tales**; famous figures: **Padmapani and Vajrapani Bodhisattvas**.
Technique: **tempera** (colours on a prepared plaster ground); rich colours, graceful lines, emotional expression; use of **shading and volume**.
Ajanta murals are the finest surviving ancient Indian paintings.

sections.heading: 3. Ellora and Other Sites
points: **Ellora caves (Maharashtra)** — **Buddhist, Hindu and Jain** caves together (a UNESCO site); the **Kailasa temple (Cave 16)** is a monolithic marvel; murals also present.
**Bagh caves (MP)** — Buddhist murals similar to Ajanta.
**Sittanavasal (Tamil Nadu)** — **Jain** murals (Pandya period).
**Badami (Karnataka)** — early **Chalukya** murals (Hindu themes).

sections.heading: 4. Later Murals — South India
points: **Chola** murals (Brihadeshwara/Thanjavur temple).
**Vijayanagara** murals (Hampi, Lepakshi — the **Veerabhadra temple, Lepakshi** ceiling paintings).
**Nayaka** period murals (Tamil Nadu) — narrative panels from epics/puranas.
The tradition continued into the medieval and Kerala mural styles.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Ajanta (Maharashtra) = Buddhist murals (Jatakas); Padmapani & Vajrapani Bodhisattvas; UNESCO site.
Ajanta technique = tempera on plaster.
Ellora = Buddhist + Hindu + Jain caves; Kailasa temple monolithic.
Sittanavasal (TN) = Jain murals; Badami = Chalukya murals.
Lepakshi (Veerabhadra temple) = Vijayanagara murals.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Ajanta = only Buddhist**; **Ellora = Buddhist, Hindu AND Jain**.
The famous Ajanta figures are **Padmapani and Vajrapani** Bodhisattvas.
**Sittanavasal (Tamil Nadu)** has **Jain** murals.
Ajanta murals use the **tempera** technique (not true fresco).
